quick.topic: Pick the method for the question
quick.summary: Why a survey could not explain why people leave, and how to match method to question.
quick.takeaway: Why needs interviews. Can they needs a test. How many needs a survey.

parts.title: Pick the method for the question

beats.line: I ran a survey to learn why people abandon setup. I got numbers, no reasons. Why?

board.text: Pick the method for the question

beats.line: Because the method follows the question. Yours was a why.
Why do they do it? Interviews. People explain in their own words.
Can they use it? A usability test. You watch them try.
How many? A survey or product data.
Interviews take a week. A survey takes an hour.
Five interviews beat five hundred answers to the wrong question.
So five interviews for why they leave. Then a survey to size it.
Right order. First the reasons, then the count.

quiz.question: You need to know why users abandon setup. Which method fits best?
options: Interviews with people who abandoned it
A count of drop offs in product data
A test of two button colours
quiz.explanation: Why questions need people explaining in their own words; counts tell you how many, not why.

quiz.question: A survey is the best method for finding out whether people can complete a task.
quiz.explanation: Watching people try the task in a usability test shows whether they can; a survey only collects what they report.
